finding.title: Deduplicate near-identical CurriculumLabels test coverage spread across 3 test files

evidence.quote: test('excludes level labels when includeLevelLabel is false', () {
test('daily targets exist for all curricula', () {

finding.why: curriculum_defaults_extended_test.dart and curriculum_labels_extended_test.dart both independently claim in their file-header doc comments to cover 'methods not yet tested' by the other files, but in fact both re-test CurriculumLabels.container, .containerSectionHeader, .level (RangeError for 0 and out-of-range), .valueWithLabel, and .fullPath (skip-null, custom-separator, includeLevelLabel=false) with near-identical test names and assertions — e.g. the 'excludes level labels' group exists verbatim in both files. curriculum_defaults_test.dart separately duplicates the CurriculumDefaults.defaultStages/defaultDailyTargets assertions that curriculum_defaults_extended_test.dart's last group re-covers. Net effect: ~1200 lines across 4 files test one 1270-line source file, with the same behavior asserted 2-3x under different names — any future change to e.g. fullPath's separator handling requires hunting through multiple files to update every duplicate, and CI burns time re-running equivalent assertions. (curriculum_label_variant_test.dart, the 4th file, was checked and found NOT to overlap — it covers distinct nusach/transliteration behavior only.)
finding.recommendation: Consolidate curriculum_defaults_extended_test.dart and curriculum_labels_extended_test.dart (partition cleanly by class — LevelLabels vs CurriculumLabels vs CurriculumDefaults — or merge into curriculum_defaults_test.dart), removing the 5+ duplicate assertion groups identified.
acceptance_criteria: No two test groups across the constants test directory assert the same production method+scenario combination
Consolidated suite's total line count is measurably smaller than the current 4-file total

finding.title: Delete dead HebrewTerms.getCurriculumDisplayName — unused, violates Rule 5 displayNameHe placement, tested twice by duplicate groups
finding.why: A repo-wide grep of lib/ finds zero production callers of HebrewTerms.getCurriculumDisplayName — the only call sites are two duplicate, identically-named test groups (lines 73 and 102, in the same file) that both just re-assert `== id.displayNameHe`, a tautology restating the implementation. The method also lives in core/constants/, not core/labels/, so its `.displayNameHe` access bypasses the Rule 5 placement boundary that the no_curriculum_display_name_bypass custom lint would flag if custom_lint weren't currently broken (per baseline). core/labels/curriculum_label.dart already has the equivalent, correctly-placed `_curriculumId!.displayNameHe` access, confirming this delegate is a superseded leftover (the doc comment even says the map it replaced was removed 'to eliminate duplication').
finding.recommendation: Delete HebrewTerms.getCurriculumDisplayName and both duplicate test groups. If Hebrew curriculum-name lookup is still needed outside core/labels/, route through CurriculumLabelRenderer per Rule 5 instead of a raw `.displayNameHe` access.
acceptance_criteria: `grep -rn getCurriculumDisplayName lib/ test/` returns no results after removal
hebrew_terms_test.dart no longer has two groups named 'getCurriculumDisplayName'

finding.title: Remove dead DuplicateCompletionException / InvalidTrackOperationException or wire them up — neither is thrown in production
finding.rule: AG-6 dead-code (Fowler speculative generality) + secondary EH-5 (hardcoded English userMessage)

evidence.quote: // Tests for DuplicateCompletionException — covers toString and userMessage.

finding.why: Repo-wide grep (lib/ and test/) shows DuplicateCompletionException is referenced nowhere outside its own definition file and its own single-purpose test file; InvalidTrackOperationException is thrown nowhere in lib/ — track_repository.dart only re-exports the type 'so existing importers of this file don't need updating,' and completion_writer.dart's current duplicate-completion handling is idempotent (silently returns the existing row, no exception thrown), confirming both exceptions' original call sites were refactored away. Both classes also bake a raw, hardcoded English message rather than a stable code (DuplicateCompletionException.userMessage is explicitly documented as 'for display in snackbars/dialogs') — if either is revived by a future feature without noticing this, it reintroduces an EH-5 violation (unlocalized English shown to Hebrew-locale users) on day one. Today the risk is purely maintenance/documentation drift: a developer debugging track-deactivation or completion-marking who searches for these classes' names will be misled into thinking they're live guards.
finding.recommendation: Delete both classes and duplicate_completion_exception_test.dart, or wire them into a live call site. If a real duplicate-completion/invalid-track-operation UI error is still needed, add a stable enum/code to a new exception rather than reviving these hardcoded-English ones.
acceptance_criteria: grep for DuplicateCompletionException/InvalidTrackOperationException across lib/ shows either a live throw+catch pair or zero results
No orphaned test file whose only coverage is a dead exception's string formatting

finding.title: Fix or delete NaturalKey.forLearnerProfile's fragile non-null-Object emptiness check — fallbackProfileId branch is effectively unreachable and untested
finding.rule: Type-safety design flaw in dead code
finding.why: profileIdOrRow is typed as non-nullable Object, so it can never be null, and Object.toString() is non-empty for every realistic value (an int, a non-empty String, or the default 'Instance of X') — the only way to hit the fallbackProfileId branch is to pass a literal empty string, which is nowhere documented as the sentinel. This reads like an attempt to model 'optional row value, else use this id' that should have used `Object?` with a null check instead of a string-emptiness check. It has zero callers repo-wide (confirmed via grep across lib/ and test/), so this has never been exercised and the bug would surface silently the moment someone starts using it expecting the fallback to work.
finding.recommendation: If kept, change the signature to `Object? profileIdOrRow` and check `== null` instead of `.toString().isNotEmpty`. If truly unused going forward, delete it along with the other 5 unused factories (see companion finding).
acceptance_criteria: If kept: a unit test constructs NaturalKey.forLearnerProfile with profileIdOrRow omitted/null and asserts the fallbackProfileId branch actually executes
If deleted: covered by the companion 'unused factories' finding's acceptance criteria

finding.title: core/time/local_day_clock.dart's currentLocalDayClock global has no compiler-enforced set/reset pairing for tests
finding.rule: SM-7 spirit (no global/static mutable singletons) / TQ-6 hermetic tests
finding.why: This mutable top-level variable backs DateTimeFactory, which is called from 15+ production sites across DAOs/repositories/mergers (e.g. track_dao.dart, a churn hotspot, calls it 8 times). Test isolation relies entirely on every caller of useLocalDayClock() remembering to pair it with `tearDown(resetLocalDayClock)` per the doc comment's 'MUST' — nothing in the type system enforces this. A test file that calls useLocalDayClock() without the tearDown pairing would silently freeze time for every later test in that file/isolate, producing flaky failures unrelated to the code under test. I checked the two actual test files that use it (only outbox_processor_test.dart and one other) and both correctly pair set/reset via `tearDown(resetLocalDayClock)`, so this is a latent, convention-enforced risk rather than a demonstrated failure today.
finding.recommendation: Add a shared test helper (e.g. `withFakeClock(seed, body)`) that calls `addTearDown(resetLocalDayClock)` itself so individual tests can't forget the reset, and migrate the existing 2 call sites to it.
acceptance_criteria: A shared test helper pairs useLocalDayClock with an auto-registered tearDown reset
Existing call sites in outbox_processor_test.dart (and any sibling) migrated to the helper
